papers.title: Hadwiger\'s Covering Conjecture in Three Dimensions
papers.abstract: Let $K \subset \R^3$ be an arbitrary convex body, that is, a compact convex subset of $\R^3$ with nonempty interior. We prove unconditionally that $K$ can be covered by eight smaller positive homothetic copies of itself: there exist a scalar $\lambda \in (0, 1)$ and translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \R^3$ such that \[ K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{8} (\lambda K + v_i). \] This resolves Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions. The proof works in Boltyanski's equivalent boundary illumination formulation and is completely self-contained. Parallelepipeds are covered directly by eight translates of $\frac{2}{3} K$. For any convex body $K$ that is not a parallelepiped, we place its centrally symmetric halved difference body $S = \frac{1}{2}(K - K)$ in John's position ($B^3 \subseteq S$) and show that the spherical average of its support function satisfies $8 \int_{S^2} h_S \, d\sigmatilde < 12$, with equality only for orthogonal cubes. Using outer polyhedral approximations together with Cauchy's planar perimeter formula, the full spherical measure of directions not parallel to any boundary segment of $K$, and lower semicontinuity of curve variation, we find a unit vector $w_* \in S^2$ whose shadow boundary $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ on $K$ itself is a continuous closed curve of $S$-length strictly less than $12$. Splitting $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ into six contiguous arcs of $S$-length strictly less than $2$ and applying Helly's theorem in $\R^3$ illuminates each arc with one direction, while $\pm w_*$ illuminate the remainder of $\partial K$. The proof was discovered using an experimental harness on top of Gemini~4 Carbon and formally verified in Lean~4.

papers.title: Helly complexes are minimal fillings
papers.abstract: We show that Helly complexes are universal minimal fillings. More precisely, if $X$ is a Helly complex, and $Y$ is a simplicial complex whose boundary is isomorphic to that of $X$ and such that the distances between the boundary vertices induced by $Y$ are at least as large as those induced by $X$, then $Y$ has at least as many vertices as $X$. The same type of inequalities hold for $i$-dimensional simplices of $X$ and $Y$ for all $i=0,1,\ldots$, i.e., for all coordinates of the $f$-vectors of $X$ and $Y$. When $Y$ is dismantlable, we show that the boundary isomorphism assumption can be weakened to a bijection between the vertex sets of both boundaries with an additional technical condition on boundary edges.

papers.title: The smallest vertex triangle in a fixed polygon
papers.abstract: Among the triangles determined by $n$ points in convex position in the unit square, one has area at most $32/n^3$. Equality is possible exactly when $4$ divides $n$, and then the maximizing point set is unique. We prove a fixed-container theorem for a class of convex $s$-gons that includes affinely regular polygons and a one-parameter family of pairwise affinely inequivalent hexagons without a centre of symmetry. If the container has equal ears of area $a$ and the tips of its directed side vectors are in convex position, the sharp bound at $n=sk$ is $a/k^3$. Its equality conditions determine every side vector of the maximizing polygon. The proof uses the area enclosed by the normalized side directions. We compare the result with the area-normalized smallest-ear theorem of Gronchi and Longinetti and give consequences for unrestricted Heilbronn configurations with 13 and 15 points.

papers.title: Weak monotonicity, Critical exponents, and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities on weighted graphs
papers.abstract: We study weak monotonicity of heat kernel and ball averaged functionals on weighted graphs, and the associated critical exponents. Under sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates, weak Bakry-\'Emery estimates for the semigroup are proved, with explicit values of the H\"older regularity exponent in the strongly recurrent case. Applications of the theory include Gagliardo-Nirenberg, Sobolev, Nash and isoperimetric inequalities on strongly recurrent graphs and their products.

papers.title: A new class of affine $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements
papers.abstract: We show that a certain class of affine hyperplane arrangements are $K(\pi,1)$ by endowing their Falk complexes with an injective metric. This gives new examples of infinite $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements in dimension $n>2$.

papers.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
papers.abstract: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element (and the empty set red). Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, right almost invariant subsets are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed, self-contained account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then give a proof of Protasov's stronger conclusion for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---showing that the full Higson corona is a singleton.

papers.title: Origametry and antagonistic heptagon graphs: the braced {35,1} and the complete {21,2}
papers.abstract: We study two planar unit-distance graphs (UDGs) that both look like heptagons but have opposite rigidity yet kindred arithmetic: the braced heptagon {35,1} (19 vertices, 35 edges) and the complete heptagon {21,2} (21 vertices, 42 edges). Neither is straightedge-and-compass constructible -- already the regular 7-gon is not, by Gauss-Wantzel -- so the natural setting is origametry: the construction of each realization by Huzita-Hatori folds, with the quadratic fold O5 (straightedge-and-compass strength) versus the cubic Beloch fold O6. The complete heptagon is over-braced and globally rigid, with a unique realization whose 42 edges are certified unit exactly, with coordinates in Q(cos pi/42), of degree 12 (minimal over all placements), containing the cubic Q(cos 2pi/7): every vertex is an origami number. It is Haugland's H21, whose two heptagram layers are the seed of the 449-vertex 5-chromatic graph of Heule and Przybocki. The braced heptagon is isostatic (minimally rigid) with thousands of non-congruent realizations and a large generic realization count N = 3869504 = 2^6 * 103 * 587; yet we prove that its unit realization is again origami-constructible. In Pegg's explicit construction the pinning angle is a root of an irreducible degree-12 palindromic polynomial whose Chebyshev reduction, an irreducible sextic, factors into quadratics over the heptagon cubic Q(cos 2pi/7); hence the coordinate field is a {2,3}-tower of degree 3*2^k, reached by one trisection followed by quadratics. The primes 103 and 587 belong to the generic complex count, not to the folded coordinates. We solve the governing cubic by folding (Lill's method and the Beloch fold), place both graphs inside Alperin's field of origami numbers, and read the fold-branch signs of the construction as mountain-valley assignments with an empirical Maekawa-type balance. All claims are checked in exact arithmetic.

papers.title: Minkowski Problems for Mixed Centro-Section Integrals
papers.abstract: Recent studies in affine convex geometry have introduced two new families of geometric measures: affine dual curvature measures and centro-section measures. Motivated by these developments, we introduce mixed centro-section integrals and establish their variational formulas. Under the subspace concentration condition, we prove the existence of solutions to the corresponding Minkowski-type problems. We further introduce mixed bi-dual $m$-intersection bodies of index $q$ and establish the corresponding sharp affine isoperimetric inequalities. The resulting mixed centro-section measures include centro-section measures and affine dual curvature measures as special cases.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for chord integrals
papers.abstract: Chord integrals are moments of chord lengths and translation-invariant averages of dual quermassintegrals. In this paper, we prove their Brunn-Minkowski inequality for $q\in[1,n+2]\cup\{n+3\}$, with equality precisely for homothetic bodies. A transfer from symmetric dual quermassintegrals to covariogram level sets gives, in dimension two, the full range $1\leq q\leq5$. For every $0<q<1$, we establish the same inequality for simplices and an explicit factor version for all convex bodies. On the other hand, rectangular perturbations give counterexamples for every $q>n+1+\beta_*$, where $\beta_*\in(2,3)$. As consequences, we obtain Minkowski inequalities and uniqueness results for chord measures. We also prove Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for affine-section integrals and mixed Riesz energies.

papers.title: Asymptotic isoperimetry for parallelohedra
papers.abstract: The smallest possible surface area of a convex translational tile of $\mathbb R^n$ approaches $\sqrt{2}$ times that of a ball of equal volume as $n\to\infty$. For the lower bound, we combine Gaussian smoothing with the Milman-Neeman multi-bubble theorem. For the upper bound, we use Siegel mean value theorem to average over lattice Voronoi cells. Our method also yields convex $\mathbb Z^n$-tiles whose orthogonal projection onto any hyperplane has volume $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, answering a question of Naor and Regev.

papers.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
papers.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is at least 2-dimensional. This strengthens the author's prior results to their optimal dimension bound and recovers Ebin's non-equivariant analogue to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

papers.title: Identification of generic polygonal domains by integral-geometric invariants
papers.abstract: We study a reconstruction problem of planar domains from non-local integral-geometric invariants. We show that a generic polygonal domain, not necessarily convex, is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean isometry, by the interpoint distance distribution (IDD), which, for convex domains, is equivalent to the chord length distribution. Using a boundary representation of the Riesz energy function, we replace the IDD of the domain by an equivalent boundary IDD weighted by the scalar product of the outer unit normals, which we call $\nu$-weighted IDD of the boundary. It enables us to reduce the problem to a one-dimensional problem. By analyzing jumps and blow-up terms of the second and third derivatives of the $\nu$-weighted IDD of the boundary, we recover the side lengths, their cyclic incidence, and the exterior angles of the polygon. This can be considered as extending Waksman's classical generic reconstruction theorem for convex polygons to non-convex setting, as well as extending generic polygonal reconstruction from directional covariogram data to a one-dimensional invariant in which directional information has been integrated out.

papers.title: SL(n)-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on polytopes
papers.abstract: All $\operatorname{SL}(n)$-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on convex polytopes in $\mathbb R^n$ are completely classified without any continuity assumptions. It is shown that the only such valuation is the moment tensor.
